display.purpose: One dominant hero statement per viewport.

body.purpose: Long-form technical guidance capped at 70 to 72 characters.

label.purpose: Short technical annotations and section cues.

mono.purpose: Ada, shell commands, API names, and generated declarations.

shadows.name: ambient-low
shadows.purpose: Floating diagram notes and interactive lift only.

shadows.name: code-float
shadows.purpose: The hero code window where it overlaps the runtime model.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: All state transitions and small transform responses.

motion.name: orbit
motion.purpose: Slow event-loop motion in the home-page runtime model.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The main next-step action on a page or section.
components.html: Start with the guide →
components.css: .ds-button-primary { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:.55rem; min-height:3rem; padding:.72rem 1.25rem; border:1px solid var(--ink); border-radius:999px; background:var(--ink); color:var(--inverse); font-family:var(--font-sans); font-size:.92rem; font-weight:620; text-decoration:none; transition:transform 200ms var(--ease-out), box-shadow 200ms var(--ease-out); } .ds-button-primary:hover { transform:translateY(-2px); box-shadow:0 1rem 2.4rem color-mix(in oklch, var(--ink) 24%, transparent); } .ds-button-primary:focus-visible { outline:3px solid var(--focus); outline-offset:4px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: A visible alternative that does not compete with the primary action.
components.css: .ds-button-secondary { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; min-height:3rem; padding:.72rem 1.25rem; border:1px solid var(--ink); border-radius:999px; background:transparent; color:var(--ink); font-family:var(--font-sans); font-size:.92rem; font-weight:620; text-decoration:none; transition:transform 200ms var(--ease-out); } .ds-button-secondary:hover { transform:translateY(-2px); } .ds-button-secondary:focus-visible { outline:3px solid var(--focus); outline-offset:4px; }

components.name: Code Panel
components.description: Executable Ada or shell material with a permanent dark syntax surface.
components.css: .ds-code-panel { margin:0; overflow:hidden; border:1px solid var(--code-line); border-radius:.9rem; background:var(--code-bg); color:oklch(91% 0.02 270); font-family:var(--font-mono); } .ds-code-panel figcaption { padding:.75rem 1rem; border-bottom:1px solid var(--code-line); color:oklch(68% 0.035 270); font-size:.72rem; } .ds-code-panel pre { margin:0; overflow:auto; padding:1.35rem; font-size:.82rem; line-height:1.75; } .ds-code-panel:focus-within { outline:3px solid var(--focus); outline-offset:4px; }

components.name: Guide Callout
components.description: A bounded operational note or constraint inside technical prose.
components.html:
!

Exact versions only. Runtime preparation fails closed for an unverified compiler.
components.css: .ds-callout { display:grid; grid-template-columns:auto 1fr; gap:1rem; padding:1.15rem 1.25rem; border:1px solid var(--line); border-radius:.9rem; background:var(--surface); color:var(--ink-soft); font-family:var(--font-sans); } .ds-callout > span { display:grid; width:1.8rem; height:1.8rem; place-items:center; border-radius:50%; background:var(--violet); color:var(--inverse); font-family:var(--font-mono); font-size:.75rem; } .ds-callout p { margin:0; } .ds-callout strong { color:var(--ink); }

components.name: API Search
components.description: Client-side filtering for generated compilation units and tagged types.
components.html: <label class="ds-search-label" for="ds-api-filter">Filter units</label><input class="ds-search" id="ds-api-filter" type="search" placeholder="Try TLS, groups, or timers">
components.css: .ds-search-label { display:block; margin-bottom:.55rem; color:var(--ink-soft); font-family:var(--font-sans); font-size:.78rem; font-weight:600; } .ds-search { width:100%; min-height:3rem; padding:.75rem 1rem; border:1px solid var(--line); border-radius:.45rem; background:var(--surface); color:var(--ink); font:1rem var(--font-sans); } .ds-search:hover { border-color:var(--violet); } .ds-search:focus-visible { outline:3px solid var(--focus); outline-offset:4px; }

narrative.overview: The visual system is a contemporary working model: precise enough to inspect, animated only when motion explains a state transition, and curious enough to reward exploration. A visible technical grid, the existing flight-and-event-loop mark, ordinary Ada syntax, and runtime topology diagrams make the system feel engineered without becoming a terminal simulation.
keyCharacteristics: A strict technical grid with varied section rhythm and asymmetric hero layouts.
A full palette in which violet means task movement and teal means readiness or completion.
Geologica carries both confident display scale and calm long-form reading.
System mono is reserved for Ada, shell commands, generated API entities, and compact indices.
Responsive motion uses transform and opacity, with a complete reduced-motion path.

rules.name: The Flight Path Rule
rules.body: Violet and teal always communicate distinct runtime states or actions. They are forbidden as interchangeable decoration.

rules.name: The Tinted Neutral Rule
rules.body: Pure black and pure white are forbidden. Every neutral remains tied to the identity's blue-violet hue.

rules.name: The Ordinary Language Rule
rules.body: Headings are direct and sentence-cased. Mono is for executable material, never a costume for technical credibility.

rules.name: The One Dominant Scale Rule
rules.body: A viewport gets one oversized statement. Body copy, diagrams, and navigation remain calm around it.

rules.name: The Mechanical Layer Rule
rules.body: A shadow must explain interaction or hierarchy. If the surface reads correctly without it, remove it.

dos: Do make runtime relationships visible through diagrams and state changes.
Do pair every capability with explicit experimental and portability limits.
Do keep ordinary Ada syntax at the center of the visual story.
Do preserve keyboard access, visible focus, color-independent meaning, readable mobile code, and reduced-motion behavior.
Do use the full palette according to the Flight Path Rule.
donts: Don't build a generic startup card wall.
Don't use faux-Victorian ornament to reference Ada Lovelace.
Don't use glassmorphism, gradient text, decorative colored side stripes, or repeated icon cards.
Don't use violet and teal as decorative substitutes for one another.
Don't imply production qualification, hard real-time behavior, universal portability, or preemptive lightweight scheduling.
